transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-05-07
- Time: 14:00 - 14:55 UTC
- Duration: 55 min
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Jared Wells (Novum Eng Mgr), Lina Park (Novum DS), Tomás Rios (Novum Security), Heather Cole (Novum Product), Marcus Lee (Novum SRE), Olivia Grant (Novum DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be coarse): Review of last week's POC metrics, discussion of final cutover runbook steps and canary/A-B rollout percentages, SLO/monitoring thresholds and rollback criteria, outstanding security/SAML and KMS questions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. we'll try to keep to 55 minutes, we have a pretty packed agenda — runbook, canary/a b plan, monitoring and rollbacks. I think Sofia will recap the timeline first.
[00:24] Sofia Alvarez: thanks Alex. Quick reminder: pilot window target is 2025-05-14 with a 4-hour cutover window, dry run this Friday. main goals today: confirm A/B split for traffic, canary ramp steps, SLO thresholds and who approves go/no-go.
[00:43] Jared Wells: sounds good. before we dive, we validated the integration with our ingestion pipeline. latency numbers on staging look close to what you reported earlier, but we saw a small error spike at peak.
[01:05] Marcus Nguyen: hey Jared, can you say the numbers? was that 95th or 99th?
[01:11] Jared Wells: 95th was around 180 ms per token equivalent for the short seq jobs; 99th spiked to 420 and that's during the evening synthetic ramp test.
[01:27] Marcus Nguyen: okay, that aligns with our profiling. we saw the same pattern — KV cache warmup and then a few tail latencies when the batcher kicked in. sometimes the transcriber here writes K V cash which is amusing.
[01:44] Lina Park: sorry, just to flag — for our prompt library the long-form scoring runs are the main pain point, that's where the 99th jumps. we can try reducing max tokens for scoring requests during the rollout.
[02:05] Alex Chen: that's a good mitigation. for canary plan we propose two phases: a small canary at 5% for 30 minutes, then ramp to 25% for an hour, then to 50% if all metrics are green, then A/B split experiments after stability.
[02:28] Heather Cole: for the A/B, we need to ensure product metric reconciliation — we want 1% accuracy drop tolerance on our ranking metric, do you have hooks to compare baseline vs new model?
[02:46] Marcus Nguyen: yes, we can stream inference outputs to your evaluation service and Redwood Optimize will compute off-platform deltas. we can also add a sampling tag to every request to tie predictions back to product events.
[03:04] Tomás Rios: on security, KMS is still open. do you support customer-managed keys and rotate without downtime? that's a requirement for us.
[03:17] Alex Chen: yes we do support CMK via KMS/HSM integrations; rotation requires a short rewrap step but we've done it in-place without service interruption in our dedicated mode. Marcus, any caveats?
[03:30] Marcus Nguyen: mainly you need to surface the key ARN and schedule the rotation outside the cutover window. we'll add a checklist step: verify key ARN, test decrypt on staging.
[03:42] Olivia Grant: on SSO—SAML flow to the console is working but we haven't tested provisioning. I tried a login earlier and got a NameID mismatch.
[03:55] Sofia Alvarez: action: Olivia to share the exact assertion and we'll triage.
[04:06] Olivia Grant: yes I will.
[04:09] [05:00] Speaker 1: uh hm, can we also talk about monitoring? what dashboards are we expecting to watch during canary?
[05:20] Marcus Nguyen: we'll provide a monitoring bundle that includes: 95/99 latency p50/p90, request error rate (5xx/4xx), token consumption delta, tail latency heatmap, model confidence distribution, and an alerts timeline for anomalies. dashboards will be in your Grafana workspace; link will be in the runbook.
[05:45] Jared Wells: what are your suggested thresholds for automated rollback? we want something we can trust, not noisy alerts.
[05:56] Marcus Nguyen: suggested hard triggers: error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes, 99th latency > 600ms sustained 3 minutes, token cost per minute increasing 20% over baseline for 10 minutes. those are conservative — we can tune.
[06:22] Lina Park: can we add a manual gating condition on model quality? e.g., if our offline eval drop > 1% on the ranking metric.
[06:33] Alex Chen: absolutely — manual quality gate will be part of the runbook steps before moving from canary to ramp.
[06:44] Heather Cole: who is the approver for the go/no-go? Product wants the final say but will need engineering and security sign-off too.
[06:56] Jared Wells: we propose Product (Heather) + Eng Manager (Jared) + Security (Tomás) for the sign-off panel.
[07:07] Alex Chen: sounds good. please confirm names in writing — we'll include them in the runbook.
[07:14] [07:40] Speaker 2: next, cutover runbook walk-through. Marcus?
[07:45] Marcus Nguyen: ok I'll read main steps briefly — pre-cutover: verify schema compatibility, confirm SAML and KMS tests, runfull smoke tests for 15 minutes at 20% of expected production RPS; stage: initiate 5% canary, monitor metrics for 30 min, if green then 25% for 60 min, then 50% for 120 min, then full ramp. rollback: immediate switchback to previous traffic router, revoke canary routing and scale up previous replica set. post-cutover: run regression checks on offline eval set and product metrics for 24 hours.
[08:30] Olivia Grant: for the router switchback how fast is the rollback? can you do sub-minute?
[08:36] Marcus Nguyen: typically we can flip routing within 30 seconds if the routing layer is healthy, but DNS and caches can add latency. the runbook includes a cache flush step.
[08:50] Tomás Rios: we need audit logs at each step for compliance — can you ensure that the runbook includes exact timestamps and who executed each step?
[09:00] Marcus Nguyen: yes, we log all orchestration events and produce an audit bundle after cutover. will add manual sign-off timestamps to the runbook.
[09:10] Heather Cole: slightly worried about the evening traffic spike you mentioned earlier. would you suggest running the cutover during our lower traffic window?
[09:23] Alex Chen: yes we recommend a low-traffic window; your earlier run suggested evenings are busy, so target a midday or early morning window that aligns with your teams being available for sign-off.
[09:36] Jared Wells: can we do two dry runs? one internal, one with the Redwood toggle?
[09:43] Sofia Alvarez: absolutely — we scheduled a dry run this Friday for the full orchestration toggle. recommend one more the day prior with a rapid rollback drill.
[09:56] [10:35] Speaker 3: pricing question popped up from procurement — will the canary ramp incur additional overage charges?
[10:45] Alex Chen: the pilot uses dedicated reserved capacity so short canaries are covered under the reserved commit for the month; if you exceed committed tokens or sustained burst beyond the plan, standard overage applies. we'll add a cost estimate table to the runbook so you can see week-of impact.
[11:05] Lina Park: also, about A/B: how do we randomize? session cookie? header? we need consistent hashing to tie sessions back to user IDs.
[11:17] Marcus Nguyen: we can do header-based routing or cookie-based. for persistent assignment across sessions we recommend a user-id hash in the routing layer — we'll provide a small snippet to implement.
[11:30] Olivia Grant: ok please include snippet.
[11:33] [12:00] Speaker 4: there was a mention of an eval spreadsheet earlier — can you re-share the baseline-vs-canary sheet?
[12:12] Alex Chen: yes, I'll share the evaluation spreadsheet and the runbook link after the call. expect link in the email.
[12:20] Heather Cole: about rollback criteria — we want one "escape hatch" that product can pull to stop the rollout without requiring devs to push code. is that possible?
[12:34] Marcus Nguyen: yes, we have a runtime toggle in the routing plane that product or ops can flip; it's role-based controlled with audit logs. we'll ensure your product user is provisioned.
[12:48] Jared Wells: small nit — can we get a runbook section that lists expected support contacts and paging order?
[12:55] Sofia Alvarez: yes, will add 24/7 on-call and escalation steps.
[13:06] Lina Park: one operational thing — what about model cache warming for long sequences? do you pre-warm top prompts?
[13:18] Marcus Nguyen: we can seed the KV cache by replaying a small percentage of typical prompts during pre-cutover. we'll document which prompts to replay and how to run them.
[13:31] Tomás Rios: from a compliance stance, we need to ensure data residency for EU requests. some of our traffic is routed to the EU; will the cutover maintain existing regional routing?
[13:45] Alex Chen: yes, we honor regional routing policies and will not cross-region traffic; canary rolling happens per-region, you can stage EU and NA separately.
[13:55] Olivia Grant: great.
[14:00] [14:30] Speaker 5: testing and observability — what retention for logs and traces?
[14:40] Marcus Nguyen: default is 30 days for traces and 90 days for request logs under the pilot plan; we can extend with an add-on.
[14:50] Heather Cole: make sure we have redaction rules for PII in logs.
[14:56] Marcus Nguyen: yep, we support PII redaction and token-level masking in transit.
[15:06] [15:40] Speaker 6: runbook versioning — how do we lock-runbook for cutover? who can edit?
[15:50] Alex Chen: we maintain the canonical runbook in your GDrive folder with version tags; only Redwood and Novum leads will have edit rights during the freeze.
[16:02] Jared Wells: can you mark the pre-cutover checklist as must-pass items?
[16:08] Marcus Nguyen: yes — we have pass/fail steps, each with owners and sign-off checkboxes.
[16:18] Lina Park: ok on data for the A/B experiments, how long will you collect stats before concluding the experiment?
[16:27] Marcus Nguyen: typically for ranking metrics we recommend 24-72 hours depending on volume; for high-volume endpoints 24 hours can be enough. we'll propose a default 48-hour window in the runbook.
[16:42] Heather Cole: want to make sure post-cutover rollback drills are scheduled — if something regresses in 12 hours we want to be able to revert.
[16:55] Alex Chen: that will be in the post-cutover monitoring cadence.
[17:02] [17:40] Speaker 7: any legal/procurement asks?
[17:50] Heather Cole: procurement will need final quotes and MSA addendum for the dedicated pilot. I can get that from your sales portal but someone will need to confirm committed capacity in writing.
[18:05] Alex Chen: I'll follow up with the formal quote and MSA addendum.
[18:12] Tomás Rios: one more security item — can we run a quick crypto review? I know you said KMS is supported but we need to confirm TLS versions and ciphers.
[18:24] Marcus Nguyen: we use TLS 1.3 and accepted ciphers; will share our security pack.
[18:33] [19:00] Speaker 8: run-of questions done, let's capture the explicit timeline and dry run details.
[19:08] Sofia Alvarez: timeline recap: dry run 2025-05-09 09:00 PT (full orchestration toggle), final load test 2025-05-08, runbook v1.2 to be shared 2025-05-09, sign-off window to be confirmed by 2025-05-12, target cutover 2025-05-14 (4-hour window).
[19:32] Alex Chen: requested owners added to action items. any other outstanding questions?
[19:40] Jared Wells: none from me.
[19:44] Lina Park: none.
[19:46] Tomás Rios: we're good.
[19:48] Heather Cole: good.
[19:50] Alex Chen: great — thanks everyone. will send notes and the updated runbook + dashboard links. recap in the email will include: exact rollback triggers, canary ramp percentages, sign-off panel, and dry-run invite.
[20:10] Meeting end.

References / artifacts mentioned:
- Runbook (shared drive): https://gdrive.company/rw/novum-cutover-runbook-v1.2 (placeholder)
- Eval spreadsheet: https://gdrive.company/rw/novum-eval-baseline-vs-canary.xlsx (placeholder)
- Staging dashboard: Grafana link will be shared

End of transcript.
